title: Subsheaves of the final etale sheaf are open subfunctors
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $H$ be a subsheaf of the final sheaf of sets on $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Then there is a unique open subscheme $W\subset S$ such that, for every etale morphism $U\to S$, $H(U)$ is a singleton exactly when $U\to S$ factors through $W$ (and is empty otherwise). For every geometric point $\bar{x}$ of $S$ [def-weil-geometric-point], $\bar{x}$ lies in $W$ exactly when the stalk $H_{\bar{x}}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is nonempty (equivalently, a singleton).

source.place: Lemma Tag 04HV (lemma-support-subsheaf-final), statement and proof; used in Lemma Tag 09XM

proof.text: For each etale object $U\to S$, the inclusion $H(U)\subseteq\{\ast\}$ makes $H(U)$ either empty or a singleton. Let $W$ be the union, over all etale objects $U\to S$ and elements of $H(U)$, of the image of $U\to S$. This is open because etale morphisms are open. The construction is independent of the chosen element, since the final sheaf has only one section.

source.place: Lemma Tag 04HV (lemma-support-subsheaf-final), proof, construction of the open locus

proof.text: If $V\to S$ is etale and $H(V)$ is nonempty, then its image is contained in $W$ by construction. Conversely, if the image of $V$ is contained in $W$, every point of $V$ has an etale neighbourhood whose map to $S$ is one of the objects used in the union defining $W$; pulling back the corresponding singleton section gives a section of $H$ on an etale covering of $V$. On overlaps these sections agree because $H$ is a subsheaf of the final sheaf, so the sheaf equalizer condition glues them to a unique element of $H(V)$. Thus $H(V)$ is a singleton exactly when $V\to S$ factors through the open subscheme $W$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 04HV (lemma-support-subsheaf-final), proof, local sections and sheaf gluing

proof.text: The open subscheme is unique: if $W'$ has the same factorization property, apply it to the open immersion $W\to S$ to get $W\subseteq W'$, and apply the stated property for $W$ to the open immersion $W'\to S$ to get $W'\subseteq W$. For a geometric point $\bar{x}$, the stalk $H_{\bar{x}}$ is nonempty exactly when some pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar{x}$ has a section of $H$, which is exactly the condition that the image point lies in the union defining $W$. Since $H_{\bar{x}}$ is a subsingleton, nonempty is equivalent to being a singleton.
